clue.text: Demonstration of professional taking the lead

indicators.note: the professional goes in front of the word 'of', leading it in the answer

parts.note: pro is the short form of professional

explanation.surface: A demonstration put on by an expert who steps up and leads.
explanation.definitionFit: Proof is evidence that establishes something, which is a demonstration of its truth.

clue.text: Weak team member transferred by coach, perhaps

explanation.surface: A feeble player gets moved on by the team's trainer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like the team's trainer, but it is the bus that carries a rider.
explanation.definitionFit: A team member who contributes nothing is carried along by others; anyone riding a coach or bus is a traveller carried by it.

clue.text: One who has new order accepted by other ranks

indicators.note: the soldiers take the reshuffled letters into their midst

parts.note: OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: putting the word new into a different order rearranges its letters

explanation.surface: Someone receives a fresh command that the rank-and-file soldiers accept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' rearranges NEW into WNE, which 'accepted by' places inside OR.
explanation.definitionFit: A proprietor is a person who possesses something, the one holding it.

clue.text: Note match that's as even as possible

parts.note: a flat is a musical note lowered a semitone
a test is an international cricket or rugby match

explanation.surface: A musical note or a sporting fixture that is about as level as it gets.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat means level or smooth, so the superlative describes something maximally level.

clue.text: Emperor recently arrived with Scot

parts.note: just, as in 'just now', means a moment ago
in means having come, as in 'the train is in'
Ian is a typical Scottish first name

explanation.surface: A ruler who has only just turned up accompanied by a Scotsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Justinian I was the sixth-century Byzantine ruler famous for codifying Roman law.

clue.text: British painter, such as Constable

explanation.surface: A British artist in the mould of the landscape painter Constable.
explanation.walkthrough: Augustus John was a Welsh portraitist; John is also Constable's Christian name, the forename of the English landscape painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Augustus John was a celebrated British portraitist, and the landscape painter Constable had the first name John.

clue.text: Mineral water in London

explanation.surface: Mineral water bottled in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mineral water' looks like one drink; split it. The second sense is the lake in Hyde Park, London.
explanation.definitionFit: A green rock-forming silicate bears this name, and so does the curving lake in Hyde Park.

clue.text: Certainly at home with legal document

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'
a deed is a signed legal document, such as one transferring property

explanation.surface: Someone sure of themselves sitting at home with a contract.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeed is an emphatic adverb expressing agreement, meaning truly or surely.

clue.text: Join together to carry out burial with torch

parts.note: to inter is to bury a body
a link is an old torch of pitch and tow carried to light the streets

explanation.surface: A funeral party carrying flames to light a burial.
explanation.walkthrough: LINK is an old word for a flaming torch, carried by link-boys who lit the way for walkers at night.
explanation.definitionFit: To interlink is to connect things to each other so they are joined mutually.

clue.text: Gentle push exposed key hidden inside

indicators.note: the key is tucked away within the word for exposed

parts.note: nude means bare, uncovered
G is a musical key

explanation.surface: A light shove reveals a key someone had concealed.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudge is a soft prod, often with the elbow.

clue.text: Heat burns silly baker

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters of heat burns are muddled into nonsense

explanation.surface: A hapless baker who keeps scorching himself in the heat of the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baker' looks like a cook, but it is someone baking in the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lying out in the sun cooks themselves, a playful sense of one who bakes.

clue.text: Old hat taken out by American

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned hat that an American takes away.
explanation.walkthrough: In American usage, to date someone is to take them out romantically.
explanation.definitionFit: Something old hat is out of fashion; an American escorted on an outing has been courted.

clue.text: Period in which no striker's caught in slips

indicators.note: the period holds the strikebreaker trapped inside it

parts.note: an era is a period of history
a rat is a worker who refuses to join a strike, a strikebreaker

explanation.surface: A cricket spell in which no batsman is out to a catch in the slips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' puts RAT inside ERA, after its R. The cricket picture (striker, caught, slips) misleads: slips are mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are listed printing mistakes, the errors or blunders in a book.

clue.text: Are the cars he heads off to go through?

indicators.note: each of the four words loses its head, its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the cars he drives off in will pass inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads off' strips A, T, C and H from the starts of Are, the, cars, he.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse is to practise, running through a performance beforehand.

clue.text: Trusty Jack, perhaps, a sort of seaman

parts.note: in card games the jack is one of the honours, the top cards
an able seaman is a rank in the navy

explanation.surface: Jack the sailor is reliable, a particular kind of seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' suggests a sailor (Jack Tar), but here it is the playing card.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone honourable has integrity, so they are reliable and can be believed.

clue.text: Rank and file radicals are on to informer

indicators.note: the radicals are placed onto the end of the informer

parts.note: grass is British slang for a police informer
in maths radicals are roots, and radical comes from the Latin for root

explanation.surface: Extremists in the party ranks have caught on to a police informer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'radicals' reads as extremists; it is maths roots.
explanation.definitionFit: The ordinary members of a movement, as opposed to its leaders, are its base.

clue.text: Result of upward mobility in British Isle?

explanation.surface: Social climbing as it happens on a British island.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascension Island is a British territory in the South Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: Rising up, as Christ did to heaven, is the outcome of moving upwards; the South Atlantic island is a British overseas territory.

clue.text: Substance found in mine's hard

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
H is the pencil-lead abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A tough material discovered in a coal mine.
explanation.definitionFit: The pith of something is its essence or core, its real meat.

clue.text: Dissident foolishly rings the Red Cross

indicators.note: foolishly suggests the letters are scattered in a careless jumble

parts.note: each ring looks like the letter O, so two rings give two Os
X is shaped like a cross

explanation.surface: A rebel recklessly phones the Red Cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foolishly' rearranges OO and THERED into HETERODO, before X. 'rings' looks like phoning, but it means two O shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Heterodox means holding unorthodox opinions, departing from accepted belief.

clue.text: Merry-maker's driver imbibing nothing

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the driver takes the nothing inside

parts.note: a car user is a motorist, someone who drives
O is the round figure zero

explanation.surface: A partygoer is a motorist who drinks nothing, the designated driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imbibing' puts O inside CAR USER, after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: A reveller is someone who drinks and celebrates noisily.

clue.text: Stretcher cases may be put on one

definitions.text: cases may be put on one

explanation.surface: Casualties may be loaded onto a stretcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stretcher cases' reads as injured people, but split it: a stretcher was a torture device, and cases sit on shelving.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval torture frame stretched its victim's limbs; a frame of shelves holds things such as luggage or bottles.

clue.text: Reduced in price, fair or inferior in quality

parts.note: down, as in 'prices are down', means lowered
a market is a fair where goods are sold

explanation.surface: Discount goods at the fair are cheap and shoddy.
explanation.definitionFit: Downmarket means cheap and aimed at the less discerning, the opposite of upmarket.

clue.text: Service provided in the Peak District

parts.note: Mass is a church service
if means provided that

explanation.surface: A church service held in an English national park.
explanation.walkthrough: The Peak District is an upland national park in northern England, here describing any district of peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A massif is a compact group of mountains, an area of peaks.

clue.text: Wild Etruscan horsemen

indicators.note: wild implies the letters of Etruscan run out of control

explanation.surface: Fierce riders from ancient Etruria.
explanation.definitionFit: Centaurs in Greek myth are half man, half horse, so literally horse-men.

clue.text: Spelling in Daily Mirror's leader

parts.note: a daily is a British cleaner who comes in each day, also called a char

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A spelling mistake in the tabloid's editorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily Mirror' looks like the newspaper, but split it: a daily is a cleaning lady and Mirror gives only M. 'Spelling' is a magic spell.
explanation.definitionFit: A charm is a magic spell or incantation, the act of casting enchantment.

clue.text: Amazement as bloody present's returned

indicators.note: the joined words are sent back the other way

parts.note: red is the colour of blood
now means the present moment

explanation.surface: Surprise that a blood-stained gift has been sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns REDNOW right round.
explanation.definitionFit: Wonder is the feeling of awe or astonishment.

clue.text: In a manner of speaking, slowly extract pound

parts.note: to draw is to pull out
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Figuratively, one gradually withdraws a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a manner of speaking' looks like 'so to speak'; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawl is lazy, drawn-out speech with prolonged vowels.

clue.text: Soundly tarred? That's settled

indicators.note: soundly signals the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: to pay a ship's seams is to coat them with pitch or tar, so tarred is payed

explanation.surface: Thoroughly smeared with tar? The matter is closed.
explanation.walkthrough: PAY is an old nautical verb: to waterproof seams with hot pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill paid is a bill settled, discharged in full.

clue.text: Unsuitable French friendship

parts.note: ami is French for friend
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Being friendly with the French is inappropriate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'friendship' must be split into friend and ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amiss is wrong or out of place.

clue.text: Money-belt for these musicians

parts.note: brass is British slang for money
a band is a strip such as a belt

explanation.surface: A money-belt bought for the musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass band is an ensemble of trumpets, cornets and tubas.

clue.text: No female runners in this park?

definitions.text: No female runners in this park?

parts.words: No female runners in this park?
parts.note: a race with no women in it has a field of only men; the park is Jane Austen's novel title

explanation.surface: A park where no women are allowed in the race.
explanation.walkthrough: In racing the field is all the runners; a field without women belongs to men. Mansfield Park is a Jane Austen novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Mansfield Park is a Jane Austen novel, and the name splits into men's runners in a race.

clue.text: The French king's about to unwind

indicators.note: the king goes round the French word

parts.note: Rex is Latin for king, as in royal signatures
la is a French word for the

explanation.surface: The French monarch is about to calm down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts LA inside REX.
explanation.definitionFit: To relax is to rest and ease tension.
